jobs.title: Customer Operations Coordinator
jobs.description:
About Broadvoice

At Broadvoice, we believe that exceptional customer experience is the cornerstone of business success. Our AI-powered contact center and communications solutions are designed to help mid-market businesses simplify service, enhance satisfaction, and swiftly resolve issues.

Our holistic approach to CX sets us apart in the market. We don’t just provide software. We offer a proven CX framework backed by hands-on support. And our platform was built to be easy to deploy, intuitive to use, and scalable without chaos.

Every role in our company contributes to our mission of providing and creating exceptional experiences. Whether you’re in product, sales, support, marketing, or operations, your work directly impacts our customers and, by extension, their customers. Collaboration, innovation, and a shared commitment to excellence define our culture.

Position Summary

As a Customer Operations Coordinator, you will be crucial in making sure every new Broadvoice customer order is complete, accurate, and ready before installation begins. You'll be the quality checkpoint between Sales and Service Delivery: verifying paperwork against the signed quote, running business credit, confirming phone numbers can be ported, and building the customer account so the Service Coordinator can start clean.

You'll also turn move, add, and change (MAC) requests into new orders, keep delayed orders and post-install follow-ups moving, and maintain the Service Delivery team's metrics reporting. You'll work closely with Sales, Service Coordinators, and customers, all in English.

Key Responsibilities

Order Review & Verification

Review every new order in Salesforce before hand-off: opportunity and account fields, seats/trunks, and MRC and NRC against the signed quote.
Confirm all documentation is signed and attached (quote, Business Order Form, LOA/COB when porting), and review order and Sales Engineer notes.
Return incomplete or mismatched orders to Sales (RTS) with a clear note on what is needed to proceed.
Verify number portability in the Bandwidth portal and, when needed, with Lumen or Inteliquent; note the result and RTS orders that cannot port.
Run business credit through Experian using Business Order Form details and email the customer when the business name or address needs clarification.

Account Setup

Build and map customer accounts in B-Hive from the signed quote, confirming signer name, title, and signed date match.
Set the account name, time zone, billing contact, and contact roles to match the Business Order Form and Salesforce.
Verify partner information and billing and technical contacts in B-Hive match Salesforce.

MAC Orders & Queue Management

Process cases from the Broadvoice MAC queue into new opportunities and TaskRay projects, updating contacts and MRC fields.
Assign MAC orders to a Service Coordinator (and TIS where applicable) and create approved NRC charges in Rev.io.
Review the Extended Timeline report so every order either moves forward or is returned to Sales, updating milestones and stage.
Follow up on open Post-Install milestones, Account Optimization items after five days, and open cases for the team.

Reporting

Keep the Service Delivery team metrics report current and delivered on schedule.

Qualifications

Experience

Experience in a customer-facing role handling orders, accounts, or service requests by phone and email, including calming a frustrated customer.
Experience updating records and tracking status in a CRM system.
Salesforce, call center, or telecom/UCaaS/VoIP order experience (number porting, carrier portals) is a plus.

Skills

A strong eye for detail: you can check a document against a checklist and catch the mismatch others miss.
Comfortable in Microsoft Excel and Outlook for tracking work and simple reporting.
Familiarity with Experian business credit checks, Rev.io billing, or TaskRay is a plus.

Soft Skills

Fluent written and spoken English, with clear writing: you can explain to a salesperson exactly what's missing and why an order is on hold.
Able to manage a queue of new orders and follow-ups at the same time without letting items go stale.
Spanish is a plus.

WHY BROADVOICE

We're not just building communication tools, we're creating the future of connection. And we need people who want to build it with us.

Own Your Growth

No cookie-cutter career paths here. Sharpen your technical edge, step into leadership, or chart a course you haven't even mapped yet. You'll get real mentorship, real resources, and the autonomy to own your outcomes.

Work on Your Terms

Remote-first isn't a perk we bolted on, it's how we operate. We trust you to deliver, wherever you do your best work.

A Team Built Different

Diverse. Inclusive. Real. This is a culture that invests in people, not just performance metrics. You'll be surrounded by people who've got your back and push you to do better work.

Impact You Can Point To

Your ideas won't get lost in the shuffle. You'll have the backing of a product that competes well, and a direct hand in transforming Broadvoice into a CX powerhouse in the channel.

Ready to help us bring our story to life?

If you're a strategic thinker who thrives on collaboration and turns ideas into results, we want to meet you. Apply now and lead the charge with us.

Broadvoice is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. Reasonable accommodation will be made as needed for individuals with disabilities.

Job description:

Requires strong attention to detail, comfort with confidential health information and HIPPA requirements, and the ability to follow up persistently with providers. Must be able to multi-task and work efficiently in a quickly changing work environment. This is an in-office position. Helpful to have experience in the medical and/or legal field or in a related area and general knowledge regarding HIPAA regulations. Position works under immediate supervision. Spanish proficiency preferred.

Key Responsibilities

Finalize preparation of state and federal court subpoenas requesting records.
Calendar deadlines to assist legal team in properly handling requests for records.
Work with process servers to secure proper process service, including follow up and retrieval of alternative provider names and addresses.
Track all requests in the case management system and proactively follow up to obtain missing or delayed records in a timely manner.

Obtain properly executed certificates from records custodians and save into case management system.
Maintain accurate logs of request dates, receipt dates, and record status.
Organize and file both digital and physical records according to firm protocols for easy retrieval.
Retain internal case dashboards up-to-date with real-time status of all requests.
Perform quality checks to ensure scanned documents are clear, complete, and correctly indexed.
Retrieve and prepare specific records for attorneys or paralegals when needed for case review, depositions, discovery responses, or trial preparation.
Draft correspondence to providers requesting records.
Protect all protected health information (PHI) and follow HIPAA and firm confidentiality rules at all times.
Perform other records-related administrative tasks as assigned.

Qualifications and requirements:

High school diploma or GED, and at least a 2-year associate degree or paralegal certificate.
At least 2 year of experience handling records in a law firm, medical office, insurance company, or healthcare setting.
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

Discretion and integrity when handling sensitive and confidential information.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant
jobs.description:
Job Description

It’s never been a more exciting time to join Vistra.

At Vistra our purpose is progress. We believe that our clients have the power to change the world and to do great things for global progress, and we exist to remove the friction that comes from the complexity of global business – to help our clients achieve progress without friction.

But progress only happens when people come together and take action. And we’re absolutely committed to building a culture where our people can do just that

We have an exciting opportunity for you to join our team as Executive Assistant. Reporting to the EVP, this full-time and permanent position is based in Bogota, Columbia and offers regional coverage, allowing you to make a significant impact to our department and its' growth.

Role Summary

The Executive Assistant provides comprehensive, proactive support to the EVP Americas, ensuring the executive's time, travel, communications, and priorities are managed efficiently. The role acts as a key point of coordination between the EVP, regional leadership teams, global stakeholders, and external partners, and plays a central part in planning regional events, preparing executive materials, and resolving day-to-day operational issues.

Key Responsibilities

Calendar and Executive Operations

Manage the EVP's calendar proactively, prioritizing commitments and resolving conflicts across multiple time zones.
Schedule meetings with internal and external stakeholders across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific, coordinating directly with executives and their assistants worldwide.
Prepare the EVP for upcoming meetings by organizing agendas, briefing materials, and follow-up actions.
Handle ad hoc requests and resolve operational issues quickly and discreetly.

Travel and Expenses

Plan and book domestic and international travel, including flights, hotels, and ground transportation, comparing options for cost and convenience.
Build detailed itineraries adjusted to local time zones.
Process and reconcile expense reports accurately and on time, in line with company policy.

Presentations and Executive Materials

Create and design high-quality PowerPoint presentations aligned with Vistra's brand guidelines for leadership meetings, town halls, and regional events.
Build organizational charts, sales leaderboards, data visualizations, and executive summaries.
Transform survey and business data into clear, presentation-ready charts and reports.

Event Planning and Coordination

Plan and execute regional events end to end, such as the Americas Regional Sales Kick Off and leadership meetings, including venue sourcing, hotel negotiations, agendas, catering, speaker materials, and attendee communications.
Design and coordinate employee engagement initiatives for teams across multiple countries, including virtual events, invitations, gift logistics, and budget tracking.
Ensure events are delivered on time and within budget.

Communication and Stakeholder Management

Serve as a liaison between the EVP and regional leaders, commercial teams, HR, and global corporate functions.
Draft and manage internal communications, invitations, and announcements on behalf of the EVP.
Maintain confidentiality in handling sensitive information related to people, strategy, and finances.

Skills And Competencies

Excellent organizational and prioritization skills, with strong attention to detail.
Ability to manage complex calendars and multiple stakeholders across global time zones.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, and Teams.
Strong presentation design and visual communication skills.
Fluent in English and Spanish, with clear and professional written and verbal communication.
Proactive, resourceful, and able to anticipate needs before they arise.
High level of discretion, professionalism, and sound judgment.

If you are excited about working with us, we encourage you to apply or have a confidential chat with one of our Talent Acquisition team members. Our goal is to make this a great place to work where all our people can thrive. We hope you join us on this exciting journey!

jobs.title: Asistente de Operaciones
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

El Asistente de operaciones reporta al Oficial de Operaciones y la gestión de compra, activos, y almacén son su responsabilidad, garantizando el cumplimiento de los estándares de IRC para cada proceso.

El cargo es clave para fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta del IRC, asegurando que todas las adquisiciones, almacenamiento, transporte, distribución y gestión de activos cumplan con los estándares de calidad, regulaciones de donantes y políticas internas de la organización. Asimismo, el Asistente de Operaciones contribuye a la implementación efectiva de intervenciones multisectoriales que incluyen seguridad alimentaria (MPCA y asistencia alimentaria), atención primaria en salud, salud reproductiva y obstétrica (SSR), salud mental y apoyo psicosocial (SMAPS), prevención de violencia de género (VBG) y educación en emergencias, garantizando que estas lleguen a las poblaciones más vulnerables con enfoque de protección, equidad de género y derechos humanos.

Responsabilidades

Realizar el proceso de adquisición de bienes y servicios con proveedores locales o en otro lugar según correspondan las actividades de los proyectos de IRC.
Realizar gestión de proveedores en Bogotá y las zonas geográficas donde programas desarrolle sus actividades (consecución, precalificación y actualización de la base de datos).
Realizar la gestión de mensajería de la oficina Bogotá.
Integrar los estándares de la cadena de suministro en las funciones operativas del cargo.
Administración de inventario de la oficina de Bogotá.
Administración de activos de la oficina Bogotá.
Apoyar las actividades de los equipos de programas según se requiera.
Apoyar las actividades administrativas de la oficina según se requiera.
Suministro y entrega de productos de aseo y cafetería según solicitud del responsable.
Apoyo en logística que se requiera en reuniones.
Apoya las operaciones de gestión de transporte del personal de la oficina Bogotá.
Desarrollar todas las asignaciones adicionales según sea necesario.

Requisitos

Técnico o Tecnólogo en Administración, Logística, Ingeniería, campo de negocios o carreras afines.
1-2 años de experiencia específica en tareas de compras, logística, almacén (cadena de suministros) en el sector humanitario.
Habilidades fuertes de desempeño organizacional, refiere a capacidad de interactuar efectivamente con personal internacional y nacional.
Manejo intermedio de herramientas ofimáticas de Microsoft.
Comprensión de ética en procedimientos de adquisición, y cumplimiento de regulaciones de donantes.
Tiene capacidad demostrada para realizar múltiples tareas y procesar información en acción para no retrasar las actividades del programa.
Le apasiona el trabajo de las ONG’s y tiene un pensamiento positivo con una actitud de "hacerlo posible y trabajar en equipo".
Usted es confiable y flexible, autodidacta y trabaja bien bajo presión y limitaciones de tiempo
Disponibilidad para viajar al campo según se requiera.

Entorno De Trabajo

Entorno de trabajo cambiante.
La presencia y movimientos de trabajo geográficamente y el alcance del programa podrían cambiar a medida que el programa crezca.

Paquete Retributivo

Contrato laboral de trabajo
Salario: $2.240.000 con Prestaciones de ley.

Professional Standards:
All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

POSITION
Administrative Assistant (Part Time)

LOCATION

BACKGROUND

Global Partnerships (GP) is an impact-first fund manager dedicated to expanding opportunity for people living in poverty. Impact-first investing means investing in a way that seeks the greatest possible social impact, while seeking to preserve capital with a modest financial return for investors. GP believes that impact-first investing has an essential role to play in advancing sustainable solutions to poverty for millions of people worldwide.

GP creates and manages impact-first investment funds that make loans and early-stage investments in social enterprises serving people living in poverty, primarily in Latin America and Africa. The GP team is comprised of mission-driven, dedicated, high-performing colleagues working primarily from offices in Seattle, Washington (USA), Bogotá, Colombia, and Nairobi, Kenya. To learn more about Global Partnerships, please visit our website at www.globalpartnerships.org.

ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The Administrative Assistant will provide critical administrative, tax and compliance support to Global Partnerships’ (GP) office in Bogotá, Colombia, and will be responsible for the day-to-day functioning of that office. The ideal candidate will be an experienced, proactive and independent administrator who assumes personal ownership on a day-to-day basis for the smooth running of the office and for keeping GP’s Colombian entity in good standing. They will exemplify GP’s commitment to mission, respect, collaboration and excellence.

The Administrative Assistant will be based in GP’s Bogotá office and will work closely with the Finance team in Seattle as well as the Bogota team and local third-party accountants. This is a part-time position, working approximately 24 hours a week. Hours are defined as in-office 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Tuesday-Thursday, however this may be adjusted occasionally based on daily projects.

Other

Embodies GP’s culture: D

jobs.title: Program & Mobilization Assistant– Generation Colombia (12-Months Fixed Term/Remote)
jobs.description:
About Generation

At Generation, we believe in the power of employment to change lives. We are a global nonprofit organization that supports adults to achieve economic mobility through employment. Generation trains and places adult learners of all ages into careers that are otherwise inaccessible, working in partnership with governments, employers, and other system actors. We also conduct original research and share data insights on high-priority global workforce transition topics to inform decision-making by workforce system stakeholders. Launched in 2015, Generation comprises a global hub (Generation You Employed, or GYE) and a network of in-country affiliates. To date, the network has 150,000+ graduates and 23,000+ employers across 50 professions and 17 countries.

When learners join Generation, 91% are unemployed, of which nearly half are long-term unemployed. Three months after completing our program, graduates have an 78% job placement rate, rising to 88% within six months. Of our employed graduates, 79% are hired by repeat employers who have previously hired Generation graduates, and 89% are in jobs directly related to the profession for which we have trained them. Employed graduates immediately earn an average of 3-4X their previous earnings. Two to five years after graduation, 77% of our alumni from upper-middle income countries continue to meet their daily financial needs and 63% can save for the future. To date, Generation’s global graduates have earned more than $1.9 billion in wages. Generation graduates typically have a secondary school background, 52% are female, 28% have dependents, and the majority identify with underrepresented communities in their country.

JOB OBJECTIVES

The Mobilization and Program Assistant will support the execution of learner recruitment and selection processes and deliver assigned operational support activities related to the training of Generation Colombia programs.

This is a 6-Months fixed-term hire with possibility of extension based on performance and confirmed funding

Key Accountabilities & Responsibilities

Make follow-up calls to applicants to ensure their progress in the process and address any questions regarding their application
Respond to both personal and Generation Colombia emails, resolving inquiries directly or escalating them as needed to ensure timely resolution
Support the selection of participants, including profile review, coordination, and conducting interviews according to established criteria.
Document each applicant’s status and progress in an organized and accurate manner using designated platforms and tools.
Support logistical processes, including the delivery of computers and other resources to selected participants.
Provide support in the organization and execution of events or informational sessions for potential participants of the program
Support the execution of events and information sessions by completing logistical tasks and on-site or virtual support activities for prospective participants.
Contribute to learner success and program delivery by collaborating with instructors and Generation teams to support technical and employability training activities for Generation Colombia programs.

ATTRIBUTES (Qualifications, Skills & Experience)

0-2 years of experience in program support, preferably in a nonprofit, start-up, or social enterprise environment
Strong communication skills. Demonstrated fluency with Spanish, English will be a plus
Experience developing program procedures and resources, with keen attention to detail
Entrepreneurial and proactive mindset to deliver against targets and seek opportunities for improvement and growth
Results-driven and able to quantify success by developing metrics/analytics
Ability to operate independently while also being a team player
Belief in Generation’s mission, preferably with experience working with disadvantaged communities

Learn more about our global teams here. If this sounds like your kind of team, we'd love to hear from you.

About The Role

We’re hiring Family Coordinators to compassionately guide families through our full service lifecycle - from contract signature to the safe return of their loved one's ashes.

In this highly accountable role, you will take extreme ownership of a high-volume book of around 100 concurrent cases. As the primary point of contact, you'll coordinate with internal teams to seamlessly manage transportation, documentation, cremation scheduling, and ashes return.

While you fully own your caseload, we are a highly collaborative team. We work together to ensure no family experiences delays during peak volumes. The ideal candidate is exceptionally organized, obsessed with the client experience, and a creative problem-solver comfortable navigating multiple systems to triage work and support others during a critical time.

What You’ll Do:

Manage a high-volume book of business, overseeing the full client life cycle from contract signature through final resolution.
Act as the dedicated point of contact, actively handling continuous inbound and outbound calls and texts throughout the workday with empathy, clarity, and professionalism.
Guide families through each step of the process while building trust, rapport, and an exceptional overall client experience.
Own key case milestones - transportation, documentation, cremation scheduling, ashes return - partnering with internal teams and vendors to keep cases moving.
Keep documentation meticulous, updating all systems promptly and accurately.
Seamlessly navigate across various platforms (HubSpot, Aircall, Slack, GSuite, internal case management system) to build case context, triage daily workflows, and solve problems efficiently.
Collaborate with teammates to maintain continuity of care - assisting with coverage, escalations, and urgent case needs as volumes shift.
Ensure smooth case handoffs and anticipate downstream impacts.

Requirements & Qualifications:

2+ years owning a caseload or book of accounts end-to-end - case management, patient or client coordination, claims handling, or similar.
Strong written and spoken English.
Exceptional capacity for high volume: you can successfully manage 100+ cases simultaneously without letting details slip, and you are meticulous about record-keeping and documentation.
Clear, calm communicator who builds trust quickly and is completely comfortable spending the majority of the workday managing communications via phone and text.
Highly accountable and proactive: you take extreme ownership of your cases, obsess over the client experience, close the loop, and act as a creative problem solver when escalations arise.
Tech-savvy and highly organized: you easily work across multiple systems to piece together context and effectively triage your daily priorities.
Energized by our mission and excited about the opportunity to help shape something new in a category that truly needs it.
A home setup that supports the work - see our tech requirements for details.

Bonus Points

Experience in environments where empathy and execution were equally important.
Spanish fluency — many of the families we serve speak it.

Details:

Remote, full-time
Compensation: $7-$14/hr (USD)
Tools: HubSpot (CRM), Aircall (phone), Slack, and our case management system
Shift: Full-time (8 hours, consistent schedule)
Days: Monday–Friday
Hours: US Day Shift: 8 a.m. - 4:30 pm Pacific Time, including a 30-minute lunch break

Why You’ll Love Working With Us:

We’re a real business, built to last. We’ve proven our model in LA and became the largest independent funeral home in California in less than two years. We’re now going national. And plan to grow for years to come.
A serious employer for global teammates. We have years of experience running distributed teams. Same 1:1s, check-ins, and career paths as our U.S. team - same expectations, same opportunities.
People stay. Regrettable turnover is very low. Don't take our word for it - read our Glassdoor reviews.
Fair compensation with real upside. Base pay benchmarked globally. Top performers consistently earn the full bonuses.
High care, high standards. Real investment in training and growth, honest feedback, no burnout culture.

About You

As a Production Coordinator, you'll keep creative work moving. You'll manage a flow of assets between copywriters, designers, and motion designers, making sure every file is where it needs to be, in the right version, at the right time. You understand how creative teams work, you catch problems before they become delays, and nothing gets lost on your watch. This is an entry-level role. You don't need years of production experience. You need to be exceptionally organized, genuinely reliable, and the kind of person who closes loops without being asked twice. If you want to build a career in production, this is the seat where you learn how it actually runs.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Payroll and Wrapbook

Own the payroll cycle in Wrapbook: project setup, onboarding, timecard collection, review, and submission
Verify timecards against deal memos and approved rates; catch and resolve discrepancies before they hit payroll
Handle final payments, kit fees, reimbursements, and wrap close-out
Be the person crew come to with payroll questions

Crew and vendor onboarding

Send, track, and complete start work packets for every crew member — tax forms, I-9 verification, direct deposit, policy sign-offs
Manage loan-out documentation, COIs, and vendor setup
Issue and track deal memos and rate confirmations so terms are documented before day one
Keep the onboarding tracker current so we always know who's ready to work and who's blocking

Receipts and reconciliation

Process and code card transactions, petty cash, and reimbursements to the right project and budget line
Chase down missing receipts and reconcile weekly rather than at wrap
Route vendor invoices for approval and hand off cleanly to accounting
Maintain cost trackers and give producers a current view of budget vs. actuals

Coordination and follow-ups

Run the follow-up system: every open item has an owner, a next step, and a date
Manage calendars, holds, travel, accommodations, and per diem tracking
Distribute production documents and confirm the people who need them have them
Keep project folders and templates organized and current
Assemble wrap books and support post-production scheduling and delivery logistics

Requirements

Exceptional organization. You have a system, you trust it, and things don't fall out of it.
Real follow-through. You'd rather send the fourth reminder than let something slip.
Attention to detail, especially with numbers, dates, and names. You understand that a small error here means someone doesn't get paid correctly.
A hard worker who's comfortable owning unglamorous work and doing it precisely.
Clear, direct, low-drama communication with crew, vendors, and internal teams.
Sound judgment about when to handle something and when to escalate — and no hesitation to raise a problem early.
Comfort with tools and spreadsheets, and the instinct to build something reusable instead of redoing the same work.
Basic familiarity with AI tools and, more importantly, the appetite to learn them quickly. We use them to draft communications, summarize documents, clean up data, and cut down repetitive work, and we'll teach you how we do it.
0–2 years of experience. Production, events, or operations background is a plus but not required.

Nice To Have

Prior experience with Wrapbook or a comparable payroll platform (Wrapbook, Media Services, Cast & Crew, ABS)
PA or production assistant experience on commercial, branded content, or social shoots
Familiarity with production accounting basics — budget line coding, POs, cost reports
Exposure to both high-volume content production and larger commercial shoots
Working knowledge of crew classification (W-2, 1099, loan-out) and standard production paperwork

is the world's first Performance Branding company, partnering with some of the biggest brands in the world to drive business growth through innovative marketing strategies. jobs.title: P&C Assistant
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

Contexto

El Comité Internacional de Rescate (IRC) responde a las peores crisis humanitarias del mundo, ayudando a restaurar la salud, la seguridad, la educación, el bienestar económico y el poder de las personas devastadas por conflictos y desastres. Fundado en 1933 a instancias de Albert Einstein, el IRC es una de las organizaciones no gubernamentales humanitarias internacionales (ONGI) más grandes del mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países y 29 ciudades de Estados Unidos para ayudar a las personas a sobrevivir, recuperar el control de su futuro y fortalecer sus comunidades. Como fuerza al servicio de la humanidad, los empleados del IRC generan un impacto duradero al restaurar la seguridad, la dignidad y la esperanza de millones de personas. Si eres una persona apasionada por el cambio y orientada a las soluciones, únete a nosotros para influir positivamente en la vida de millones de personas en todo el mundo y lograr un futuro mejor.

Resumen Del Puesto

Bajo la supervisión de la Gerencia de Personas y Cultura (P&C), el/la Asistente de Personas y Cultura brinda apoyo técnico y administrativo a los procesos de gestión del talento humano para la respuesta Colombia–Venezuela, con especial énfasis en la gestión documental y el cumplimiento de los estándares institucionales y de los donantes. Es responsable de asegurar la adecuada organización, actualización, control y trazabilidad de la documentación asociada al ciclo de vida del colaborador, apoyando los procesos de reclutamiento, contratación, inducción y retiro, así como la preparación de auditorías y revisiones de cumplimiento. Adicionalmente, contribuye a la ejecución de iniciativas de bienestar y cultura organizacional, promoviendo la eficiencia y calidad de los procesos de Personas y Cultura.

Responsabilidades

Reclutamiento, selección y gestión documental

Brindar soporte integral a los procesos de reclutamiento y selección, coordinando actividades operativas y administrativas bajo los lineamientos del responsable de Personas y Cultura y garantizando el cumplimiento de las políticas, procedimientos y estándares institucionales del IRC.
Coordinar la programación de entrevistas, pruebas, llamadas y demás actividades asociadas a los procesos de selección, realizando seguimiento oportuno con candidatos y equipos contratantes.
Elaborar, consolidar y mantener actualizada la documentación y registros asociados a los procesos de reclutamiento y selección, incluyendo actas, matrices de seguimiento, bases de datos y reportes.
Gestionar y dar seguimiento al proceso de ATC de trabajadores, consultores, voluntarios y demás terceros, asegurando el cumplimiento de los requisitos establecidos.
Verificar, recopilar y validar la documentación requerida para la contratación, renovación y vinculación de personal y terceros, garantizando la integridad, vigencia y conformidad de los expedientes.
Administrar y mantener actualizado el archivo físico y digital de los procesos de selección y contratación, asegurando la correcta clasificación, trazabilidad, confidencialidad y disponibilidad de la información conforme a los requisitos institucionales, legales y de los donantes.
Realizar controles periódicos de calidad documental para asegurar que los expedientes del personal estén completos, actualizados y listos para procesos de auditoría interna y externa.

Administración de personal e inducción

Coordinar los aspectos administrativos de los procesos de inducción y reinducción, garantizando la preparación de documentación, registros y seguimiento a las actividades correspondientes.
Apoyar la preparación y seguimiento de solicitudes de compra (PR), formularios de pago (PRF) y demás documentos administrativos requeridos por el área de Personas y Cultura.
Gestionar la elaboración, actualización y archivo de certificaciones laborales, comunicaciones y demás documentos relacionados con la administración de personal.
Dar seguimiento a la recepción y organización de documentos relacionados con novedades de personal, contrataciones, renovaciones y terminaciones contractuales.

Gestión de archivos, cumplimiento y auditoría

Ser responsable de la administración integral del archivo físico y electrónico de Personas y Cultura para Colombia y Venezuela, garantizando el cumplimiento de la legislación laboral, las políticas organizacionales, los requisitos de los donantes y los estándares de auditoría.
Implementar controles documentales que permitan asegurar la trazabilidad, consistencia y adecuada conservación de la información laboral durante todo el ciclo de vida del colaborador.
Mantener actualizados los expedientes de empleados, voluntarios, consultores y terceros, verificando de manera periódica la existencia de documentos obligatorios y alertando sobre vencimientos o información faltante.
Preparar y consolidar documentación e información requerida para auditorías, revisiones internas, procesos de cumplimiento y requerimientos institucionales.

Hojas de tiempo y procesos de personal

Administrar y monitorear el proceso de recopilación, validación y archivo de hojas de tiempo del personal, garantizando el cumplimiento de las políticas institucionales y los requisitos de los donantes.
Realizar seguimiento con empleados, supervisores y áreas involucradas para asegurar la entrega oportuna y correcta de las hojas de tiempo.
Garantizar que todas las hojas de tiempo y soportes relacionados se encuentren debidamente firmados, organizados y archivados de acuerdo con los procedimientos establecidos.
Gestionar y archivar la documentación relacionada con procesos de desvinculación, incluyendo entrevistas de salida, liquidaciones, paz y salvos y demás soportes requeridos, asegurando la integridad y conservación de los expedientes.

Reporta a: Gerencia de Personas y Cultura.

Planificar, organizar, dirigir, desarrollar y aplicar el SG-SST y como mínimo una vez al año realizar su evaluación.
Informar a la alta dirección sobre el funcionamiento y los resultados del SG-SST.
Promover la participación de todos los miembros de la empresa en la implementación del SG-SST.
Coordinar con los jefes de las áreas, la elaboración y actualización de la matriz de identificación de peligros, evaluación y valoración de riesgos y hacer la priorización para focalizar la intervención.
Validar o construir con los jefes de las áreas los planes de acción y hacer seguimiento a su cumplimiento.

Entorno de trabajo cambiante.

La presencia y movimientos de trabajo geográficamente y el alcance del programa podrían cambiar a medida que el programa crezca.

Estándares

Estandares de conducta profesional: los trabajadores de IRC y IRC deben adherirse a los valores y principios descritos en IRC Way-normas para la conducta profesional. Estos son integridad, servicio y rendición de cuentas. De acuerdo con estos valores, el IRC opera y aplica políticas sobre la protección del beneficiario contra la explotación y el abuso, la salvaguardia del niño, el acoso en el lugar de trabajo, la integridad fiscal y anti-represalias.

Igualdad de género: IRC se compromete a reducir la brecha de género en posiciones de liderazgo. Ofrecemos beneficios que proporcionan un entorno propicio para que las mujeres participen en nuestra fuerza de trabajo, incluido el permiso parental, los protocolos de seguridad sensibles al género y otros beneficios y subsidios de apoyo.

Igualdad de oportunidades del Empleador: IRC es un empleador de igualdad de oportunidades. El IRC considera a todos los solicitantes sobre la base del mérito sin tener en cuenta la raza, sexo, color, origen nacional, religión, orientación sexual, edad, estado civil, estado de veterano, discapacidad o cualquier otra característica protegida por la ley aplicable.

PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS

All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Bilingual Scheduling & Intake Specialist
jobs.description:
Remote | Personal Injury | Part-Time, 30 hours/week initially | $7/hour

About The Role

We are seeking a compassionate, reliable, and highly organized Bilingual Scheduling & Intake Specialist
to support a growing personal injury medical practice.

This role will manage the patient journey from scheduling through pre-visit intake and documentation. You will serve as an extension of the physician by helping patients feel heard, gathering detailed medical information, ensuring required forms are completed, and keeping communication and scheduling workflows organized.

The practice operates exclusively on personal injury liens and Letters of Protection
, with no cash or traditional insurance billing.

Key Responsibilities

Patient Scheduling & Appointment Coordination

Manage end-to-end patient scheduling and ensure appointments are accurately entered and tracked.
Send appointment reminders and confirmation messages through text or other approved communication channels.
Monitor upcoming appointments and proactively address scheduling changes, cancellations, or outstanding patient requirements.

Patient Intake & Clinical Documentation

Conduct detailed phone intake calls approximately 2 to 3 days before each patient's appointment.
Ask structured medical questions, listen carefully to patient histories and complaints, and help patients feel genuinely heard.
Accurately type and document intake conversations and upload completed information into the appropriate practice system.

Lien Forms & Patient Documentation

Send patients required lien, Letter of Protection, consent, and signature forms through text or email.
Follow up with patients to ensure all required documents are signed before their scheduled appointment.
Verify that completed documentation is received, uploaded, and available to the practice before the visit.

Inbox & Patient Communication

Monitor and help manage the clinic's shared email inbox and incoming patient communications.
Respond appropriately to routine patient inquiries and identify messages that require escalation to the physician.
Communicate with patients in a warm, professional, and empathetic manner, especially when they are anxious, frustrated, or concerned.

Clinical Triage & Escalation

Recognize concerning symptoms during patient conversations using established clinical guidance and protocols.
Direct patients experiencing identified emergency symptoms to seek appropriate emergency medical care instead of waiting for an office response.
Escalate clinical concerns, unusual situations, or questions to the physician when additional guidance is required.

Process Documentation & Cross-Coverage

Help document workflows and contribute to the development of SOPs and a practice playbook during the first 90 days.
Learn the Patient Follow-Up & Legal Records Specialist's core workflows to provide backup coverage when needed.
Support additional administrative or patient communication responsibilities during periods of increased workload or team absence.

Required Qualifications

Fully fluent in English and Spanish, including confident verbal communication in both languages.
Nursing, clinical, allied-health, or other healthcare background with experience gathering patient histories and medical complaints.
Strong knowledge of common medical terminology.
Excellent listening, interviewing, documentation, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to communicate empathetically with patients and make them feel heard and cared for.
Strong attention to detail and consistent follow-through.
Comfortable working independently while knowing when to escalate concerns.
Able to work consistently during Mountain Time business hours.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience in personal injury, specialty medicine, medical reception, or clinical intake.
Experience working with bilingual or Spanish-speaking patient populations.
Familiarity with Letters of Protection, lien-based medical practices, or legal-medical documentation.

Tools & Systems

GoLean Productivity Tool for productivity and call-duration monitoring.
GoLean Private Network for secure access to patient records and practice systems.
Practice scheduling, email, texting, documentation, form, and patient intake systems. Specific platform names were not identified during the discovery call.

What Success Looks Like

Patients are scheduled accurately, receive timely reminders, complete required lien and signature forms, and have their intake completed 2 to 3 days before their visit.
Patient conversations are warm, thorough, and clinically appropriate, with important medical complaints and histories documented accurately and escalated when necessary.
The physician can rely on you to consistently manage scheduling, intake, inbox communication, and documentation without tasks being missed, while also providing backup support to the second VMA when needed.

jobs.title: Travel Coordinator
jobs.description:
Who is UJV?

Planning and managing a 5-star vacation from scratch requires expertise, cleverness, and a genuine passion for detail. That's what UJV is all about. UJV is a service-driven team of experts that work behind the scenes, engineering luxury travel experiences for advisors globally, so they can grow their business and fully satisfy their exclusive clients.

We are the luxury travel advisor’s right hand. How?

UJV is a team of travel experts that advises and supports luxury travel advisors worldwide.
We work behind the scenes as allies of top luxury travel advisors, to offer a 5 Star experience for their clients.
We offer travel advisors the knowledge and tools needed to grow their business and better serve their exclusive clients.
We offer an experience-centered service based on passion, expertise, integrity
and attention to detail.
We are willing to do the hard work in order to see our clients shine.

Role Mission

Internal Title: Travel Logistics Coordinator

The Travel Coordinator
plays a key role in supporting UJV’s growth by managing the logistical details that drive our business development efforts. From coordinating industry events and familiarization (FAM) trips to organizing reporting, invoices, and client gifting, this role ensures that every initiative runs smoothly. The Coordinator will work closely with the Head of Business Development, Directors, and partners to deliver seamless experiences that strengthen relationships and support long-term business success.

Responsibilities

Event Coordination

Organize and coordinate company participation in networking events, trade shows, and conferences, including managing invitations, RSVPs, registrations, and event materials.
Ensure logistics are handled in advance and follow-up is completed afterward.

FAM Trips (Familiarization Trips)

Work closely with Product and UJV’s partners to develop detailed itineraries that include flights, accommodations, transportation, and activities.
Utilize FamGuru for itinerary management and agent communication.
Conduct post-trip follow-up by gathering feedback from participants to strengthen relationships and encourage repeat business.
Maintain accurate and organized records of all client information, bookings, invoices, and financial transactions related to FAMs and other events.

General Support

Support client gifting (flowers, e-gift cards, branded items) and assist with year-end gift purchasing.
Assist in the organization and preparation for webinars (registration, Zoom setup, materials).
Collaborate with the Head of Business Development and Directors on special projects and tasks as needed.
Assist with override tracking and reporting. Organize and maintain records of invoices and signed agreements.
Run production reports from Tableau and other platforms to support account reviews and client meetings.

Qualifications

2–4 years of experience in coordination, logistics, events, or a similar role (hospitality, travel, or business development support experience is a plus).
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Excellent communication skills, with fluency in English (written and spoken).
Tech-savvy with experience using platforms such as Zoom, CRM tools, reporting dashboards (Tableau experience preferred), and itinerary management tools (FamGuru experience is a plus).
Detail-oriented with strong record-keeping and documentation habits.
Comfortable working both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
A proactive problem-solver who can anticipate needs and follow through on tasks with minimal oversight.

jobs.title: SOX Controls and Compliance Manager
jobs.description:
The SOX Controls and Compliance Manager will play a critical role in ensuring the company's compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) requirements. This individual will be responsible for designing, implementing, maintaining, and testing internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR), as well as coordinating with management, internal and external auditors for any required remediations. The Manager will drive the continuous improvement of the SOX program, promote a strong control environment, and provide expert guidance to stakeholders across the organization.

SOX Program Management:
Lead the planning, execution, and reporting of the annual SOX compliance program.
Develop and maintain comprehensive documentation, including process narratives, flowcharts, control matrices, control designs and risk assessments.
Coordinate with process owners to identify and document control changes and ensure controls are updated as business processes evolve.
Manage the relationship and deliverables with external audit partners related to SOX testing and inquiries.
Prepare and present SOX findings, assertions, and program status to senior management.
Assist and provide expert guidance to management in the implementation and design of controls and overall SOX compliance.

Internal Control Design & Effectiveness:
Oversee the design, implementation, and testing of internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR), including both business process controls and IT General Controls (ITGCs).
Conduct walkthroughs to understand key business processes, identify risks, and assess the effectiveness of control design.
Perform and/or oversee the testing of controls for operational effectiveness, ensuring adequate coverage and proper documentation of results.
Evaluate control deficiencies, identify root causes, and work with control owners to develop and monitor remediation plans to ensure timely resolution.
Rationalize and optimize controls, seeking opportunities for automation and efficiency improvements while maintaining compliance.

Risk Assessment:
Lead or participate in the annual SOX risk assessment and scoping exercises to identify in-scope processes, accounts, and systems.
Assess the impact of new systems, processes, and business changes on the internal control environment and update controls accordingly.

Collaboration & Communication:
Serve as a key liaison between internal audit, process owners (Finance, IT, Operations, etc.), and external auditors.
Provide guidance and training to control owners and stakeholders on SOX compliance requirements, internal control best practices, and the importance of a strong control environment.
Foster a culture of compliance and continuous improvement across the organization.

Policy & Procedure Enhancement:
Review and enhance existing policies and procedures related to internal controls and SOX compliance.
Stay abreast of changes in PCAOB rulemaking, SEC requirements, and industry best practices to ensure the SOX program remains current and effective.

Special Projects:
Assist with other compliance audits and special projects as necessary or assigned.
Support initiatives related to data gathering and validation for ESG disclosures and other regulatory requirements.

Education:
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field required.
CPA, CIA, CISA, or other relevant certifications highly preferred.

Experience:
5+ years of progressive experience in internal audit, public accounting (audit assurance), or SOX compliance roles.
Demonstrated experience managing SOX programs in a public company environment.
Strong understanding of internal control frameworks (e.g., COSO), auditing standards (PCAOB), and SEC regulations.
Experience with IT General Controls (ITGCs) and a sound understanding of IT platforms, applications, and related technology.

jobs.description:
Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

The Compliance Specialist – AI Governance & Privacy Operations will support Medtronic's AI governance program by assessing AI solutions, identifying risks, and partnering with global stakeholders to promote the compliant and responsible use of AI across the organization. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to a growing strategic function while collaborating with business, legal, privacy, compliance, and technology teams worldwide. This position is based in Bogotá, Colombia, and follows a hybrid work model.

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:

Conduct AI Assessments for Business Use, evaluating AI solutions for governance, privacy, compliance, security, transparency, accountability, and responsible AI considerations
Review AI use cases, models, tools, and third-party AI solutions to identify risks and applicable governance requirements
Partner with Privacy, Legal, Information Security, Compliance, Data Governance, and business stakeholders to evaluate and mitigate AI-related risks
Assess third-party vendors and external partners as part of AI and privacy risk assessment activities
Document assessment outcomes, risk analyses, recommendations, and governance requirements
Support remediation efforts and track risk mitigation actions through closure
Assist with Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), Third-Party Risk Assessments (TPRAs), and related privacy governance activities
Support continuous improvement of AI governance frameworks, assessment methodologies, and operational processes
Monitor emerging AI technologies, regulations, standards, and industry best practices
Prepare reports, metrics, and presentations related to AI assessment activities and governance program effectiveness

Required Knowledge and Experience:

Bachelor's Degree required; Law Degree strongly preferred
Experience in compliance, privacy, risk management, governance, legal, data protection, technology risk, AI governance, or related fields
Experience conducting risk assessments, compliance reviews, governance evaluations, privacy assessments, or similar activities
Familiarity with AI governance, AI risk assessment, responsible AI principles, and emerging AI technologies.
Knowledge of privacy and data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA/CPRA, LGPD, PIPEDA, or PIPL) and AI governance frameworks is preferred
Experience with governance, risk, and compliance platforms such as OneTrust, ServiceNow, Archer, LogicGate, or similar tools
Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts into business and compliance risks
Ability to work effectively with global stakeholders and cross-functional teams
Strong verbal and written communication skills
English proficiency at B2 level or above

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

About The Role

The Global Health Office (GHO) Health and Specialist & Site Advisor is a subject-matter expert. This expert serves as the primary Health & Safety contact for our Bogota site, reporting to our Regional H&S Manager.

In this onsite role, you will support the local implementation of EA health and safety policies and governance requirements in Colombia. You will also manage site-specific health and safety services, training, SG-SST requirements, and risk assessments for our Colombia teams. You will partner with teams to ensure compliance, support safety programs, and foster a culture of health within our Bogota studio.

Responsibilities

Create and deliver training programs, including annual evacuation exercises and role-specific evacuation team training, to ensure preparedness and compliance.
Maintain Colombia health and safety communications, collaborating with teams to ensure content meets EA standards and is communicated to employees and partners.
Collaborate across teams, including HR, Legal, Workplace/Facilities, IT, and Physical Security, to integrate governance and risk management into local site operations.
Anticipate and adapt health and safety programs to changes in the internal and external environment, such as regulatory updates or health risks.
Support SG-SST execution and documentation, including audit readiness, compliance records, workplace inspections, psychosocial risk management, emergency preparedness, ARL coordination, COPASST, and continuous improvement.
Present safety Indicators and compliance updates to local and regional partners.
Manage health and safety services for the Bogotá studio, ensuring a system for managing safety-related risks.
Deliver local health & safety programs with operational support and oversight.
Maintain safety-related documentation, review for updates, and coordinate the distribution of information to relevant local teams.
Provide subject matter expertise (SME) for site-specific safety meetings and risk assessments, partnering with local partners to resolve internal and external concerns.

Qualifications

4 or more years of experience in Health & Safety, SG-SST, organizational governance, or a related field.
Experience managing health and safety in a corporate office or studio environment.
Knowledge of Colombian SG-SST requirements, including audits, inspections, risk assessments, emergency preparedness, ARL coordination, and COPASST.
Experience delivering training and guidance to diverse partners, including emergency response or safety protocols.
Project management and documentation skills, with the ability to organize records, action plans, and tracking results.
Valid Colombian SST License and 50-hour SG-SST certification required.
Advanced English proficiency required to communicate with team members.

From leadership that brings out your potential, to creating space for learning and experimenting, we empower you to do great work and pursue opportunities for growth.

jobs.title: Risk Governance Analyst
jobs.description:
About Us

Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

The Risk & Controls Analyst is an individual contributor role responsible for supporting second-line-of-defense risk governance by providing independent oversight, effective challenge, and credible assurance over operational risk management and control performance across Client Care and related operational processes. The role partners with business stakeholders to identify emerging risks, assess control design and operating effectiveness, and drive timely remediation of control gaps and issues.

The Risk & Controls Analyst analyzes trends, investigates drivers of control failures, and influences operational change by translating risk signals into clear, actionable insights. The analyst collaborates with Operations and risk partners to support Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) activities by validating risk/control narratives, challenging inherent and residual risk assessments, and ensuring control documentation and evidence align with governance standards; the role also tracks corrective action plans through closure.

This role leverages analytics, visualization platforms, and (where applicable) AI-assisted monitoring to surface non-obvious risk and control insights, validate automated outputs for accuracy and defensibility, and deliver decision-ready narratives that inform leadership priorities, risk appetite decisions, and investment in control enhancements.

Responsibilities

Risk & Control Monitoring

Execute control monitoring activities (e.g., sample‑based reviews, exception reviews, and control self‑checks) to confirm adherence to documented procedures, policies, and control requirements.
Support control testing and validation (including automated or AI-assisted monitoring where applicable) by reviewing outputs, investigating exceptions, and providing structured feedback to improve detection logic and alert accuracy.
Identify control gaps, compliance risks, process breakdowns, and potential operational risk events; document observations with clear evidence and defined escalation paths.

RCSA & Issue Management

Facilitate and provide effective challenge for RCSA deliverables by partnering with process owners to validate process flows, risks, controls, ownership, and supporting evidence; ensure documentation meets governance and auditability standards.
Review and challenge control design and operating effectiveness assessments; identify gaps, risks, and control enhancement opportunities aligned to risk appetite and policy expectations.
Oversee issue and corrective action plan tracking, providing independent challenge on root cause, action quality, target dates, and sustainability of fixes; escalate aging or high‑risk items as needed.
Prepare second‑line governance reporting for RCSA reviews, summarizing key changes, emerging risks, control performance, issue themes, and remediation status; escalate matters requiring leadership decisions.

Consultative Partnership & Influence

Analyze risk and control performance data across segments, channels, and time to identify trends, systemic issues, key risk indicators (KRIs), and emerging risk themes.
Translate control observations into measurable business impact, connecting failures to process, policy, technology, or behavioral drivers and quantifying exposure where possible.
Compile, analyze, and deliver recurring risk and control reporting (dashboards, themes, exception trends, and remediation status) to Client Care leadership and risk stakeholders.
Partner with Operations and functional leaders to provide an independent risk perspective and effective challenge, validating that proposed remediations address root cause and strengthen the control environment.

Risk & Controls Technology Enablement

Leverage analytics and monitoring tools (e.g., Copilot, exception analytics, topic mining, speech/text analytics where applicable) to accelerate risk identification while validating outputs for accuracy, completeness, and defensibility.
Identify gaps in automated monitoring and AI/rule-based control logic; support governance efforts to improve detection, thresholds, documentation, and exception handling.
Apply risk‑based methodologies to prioritize high‑risk activities for monitoring and testing, focusing effort where exposure and customer impact are greatest.

Communication & Presentation

Synthesize complex risk and control findings into clear narratives that articulate what happened, the root cause, the impact/exposure, and the recommended corrective actions.
Deliver concise insight briefs and executive‑ready materials (e.g., dashboards, issue logs, and remediation status updates) that drive understanding, alignment, and action.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Experience performing operational risk, compliance, audit, testing, and/or control monitoring activities in an operations environment (payments and/or customer service experience a plus).
Demonstrated ability to execute control testing/monitoring (manual and/or automated) including evidence collection, exception documentation, and follow‑up under moderate supervision.
Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills with the ability to assess risk, identify trends and root causes, and distinguish isolated errors from systemic control issues; audit-minded approach.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Microsoft Copilot) and experience navigating multiple systems and data sources.
Ability to clearly document control testing results, maintain issue/action logs, communicate risk insights, and collaborate effectively with cross‑functional stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Risk management experience supporting or executing RCSAs, including process mapping, risk/control identification, inherent and residual risk assessment (including scoring/ratings), and review/challenge of control design and operating effectiveness. Knowledge of GORO (IBM Pages) for RCSA is a plus.
Proficiency with data visualization and analytics tools (e.g., Power BI, Power Automate, Tableau) to build dashboards and performance reporting. Basic experience with AI is a plus.
Experience translating monitoring outputs into prioritized corrective actions, control enhancements, training/coaching recommendations, and process improvements.
Familiarity with automated monitoring, exception management, and speech/text analytics that can be applied to risk identification and control validation.

jobs.title: Internal Controls Senior WACAM
jobs.description:
Job Description

Are You Ready to Make It Happen at Mondelēz International?

Join our Mission to Lead the Future of Snacking. Make It Uniquely Yours.

You will partner with financial and operational management in a limited geographic or process area to understand and enhance internal control environments, risks, and mitigation activities to minimize the risk of financial losses, operational inefficiencies and statutory non-compliances caused by the lack of controls or effective governance. You will conduct deep-dive analyses on risk areas, provide training on controls, and support management in Control Self-Assessments(CSA) and SOX activities. In addition, you will manage the locally based Internal Control Managers.

How You Will Contribute

You will:

Manage the Internal Controls team and processes for a country/process including partnering with management to optimize the internal control environment through design, training, monitoring (CCM) and testing (SOX, CSA)
Contribute to a strong controls and compliance environment at Mondelēz International by providing expert assessment of our policy and controls effectiveness and organization compliance. You will also provide training on policy and controls
Conduct advisory reviews on the identified risk areas. You will also support management in SOX testing/ driving the Control Self-Assessment (CSA)exercise. In addition, you will address ad hoc requests made by management as it relates to process, risks and controls
Drive for harmonization, efficiencies and improvements to ways of working and build a mindset of continuous improvement within the Internal Controls team
Build a high-performing team through coaching and developing auditors. You will also contribute to Mondelēz International’s Finance talent agenda in your area of scope

What You Will Bring

A desire to drive your future and accelerate your career. You will bring experience and knowledge in:

TECHNICAL EXPERTISE in internal controls and audit practices including expertise in risk/control frameworks, enterprise risk management processes, financial policies and procedures, U.S. GAAP/IFRS and SOX requirements
BUSINESS ACUMEN with an understanding of business practices within the country with knowledge in financial reporting, sourcing, supply chain, marketing, information systems, sales, shared service and customer service operations. Significant and relevant external/internal audit experience in a Big Four accounting firm and/or in a large global corporation. General understanding of enterprise resource planning applications
LEADERSHIP SKILLS including proven business partnering and communication skills across a large global, public company; experience working as a finance leader managing a diverse, cross-functional and business partner teams to drive compliance environment
GROWTH/DIGITAL MINDSET and the ability to identify strategic opportunities and leverage technology to improve operational efficiency and effectiveness
INTEGRITY and sound judgement in all decisions and interactions aligned with our values and policies and external regulations

More About This Role

Oversee the Internal Controls function for multiple countries/processes across the WACAM region, acting as a strategic partner to senior leadership to strengthen the internal control environment. This role is responsible for designing, implementing, and monitoring control frameworks (SOX, CSA, CCM), driving compliance, and building a high-performing team. The Senior Supervisor operates as the subject matter expert in internal controls, providing thought leadership on risk mitigation, process optimization, and continuous improvement across the organization — with a strong focus on Supply Chain and end-to-end business operations in consumer goods/manufacturing environments.

Key Accountabilities:

Lead the Internal Controls team for multiple countries/processes, acting as a strategic partner to senior leadership to optimize the internal control environment through control design, training, continuous monitoring (CCM), and compliance frameworks (SOX, CSA).
Contribute to building a robust controls and compliance environment at Mondelēz International by providing expert assessment of corporate policies, monitoring their effectiveness and adherence across the organization, and delivering training on policies and control procedures.
Conduct risk-based control reviews to advise on identified risk areas. Partner with senior management throughout SOX testing cycles and lead the Control Self-Assessment (CSA) exercise. Address ad-hoc requests from leadership related to processes, risks, and controls.
Drive harmonization, efficiency, and continuous improvement across internal control processes and ways of working, fostering a mindset of operational excellence within the Internal Controls team.
Build and develop a high-performing team through structured training, coaching, and professional development initiatives. Contribute to Mondelēz International's Finance Talent Development Program within the scope of the role.

Strategic Control Leadership

Lead and manage the Internal Controls team for multiple countries/processes across WACAM, acting as a strategic partner to senior leadership to optimize the internal control environment through design, training, monitoring (CCM), and controls execution (SOX, CSA).
Define and drive the annual internal controls strategy and roadmap, ensuring alignment with global Mondelēz standards and regional business priorities.
Provide expert assessment of policies, control effectiveness, and compliance across the organization, proactively identifying gaps and recommending remediation plans.
Lead the SOX testing program end-to-end: scoping, planning, execution, deficiency evaluation, and remediation tracking — collaborating directly with external auditors and global IC leadership.

Risk Management & Business Advisory

Conduct comprehensive risk-based reviews across business processes, going beyond SOX checklist-based audits to include deep-dive site visits (plants, distribution centers, warehouses) and hands-on business interaction.
Serve as a trusted advisor to senior management on process risks, control design, and operational efficiency — particularly within Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Logistics processes.
Lead the Control Self-Assessment (CSA) exercise across the region, ensuring business ownership of controls and driving accountability at all levels.
Address ad-hoc management requests related to process reviews, risk assessments, and special investigations with a solution-oriented approach.

Process Excellence & Continuous Improvement

Drive harmonization, standardization, and efficiency improvements across internal control processes, systems, and ways of working across multiple WACAM countries.
Develop and embed a continuous improvement mindset within the IC team and across business stakeholders, leveraging data analytics and automation to enhance control monitoring.
Lead cross-functional projects to redesign or strengthen control frameworks in response to organizational changes, system implementations, or regulatory updates.

Industry Experience

Strong preference for candidates with 10+ years of hands-on experience in Internal Controls within manufacturing, consumer goods (CPG/FMCG), or retail industries. The candidate must have built their career within the internal controls function of a multinational company — experience limited exclusively to professional services firms (Big 4, consulting, BPO) does not meet the requirements for this role.
Scope & Control Expertise
We are looking for a seasoned professional whose experience goes well beyond SOX checklist-based control testing. The ideal candidate has led comprehensive, risk-based control reviews, conducted on-site visits to plants, distribution centers, and warehouses, and has a proven track record of engaging directly with the business to assess, design, and strengthen the control environment. This is a hands-on, business-facing role — not a desk-only position.
Functional Focus
The role is centered on Supply Chain controls — procurement, manufacturing, logistics, warehousing, and distribution. The candidate must demonstrate deep understanding of end-to-end Supply Chain processes and the ability to design practical, business-enabling controls within operational environments.

Language Skills

Fluent English (B2 level minimum) is mandatory and non-negotiable. The role requires daily interaction with regional and global stakeholders, including presenting to senior leadership, drafting reports, and leading cross-functional meetings — all conducted in English. Candidates below C1 level will not be considered. Native or fluent Spanish is also required. Portuguese is a plus.

Leadership & Soft Skills

This is a people leadership role managing a team of 4-5 IC professionals. The ideal candidate demonstrates:
Exceptional communication skills — able to translate complex control concepts into clear, actionable language for both technical and non-technical audiences.
Strategic thinking with operational execution — sees the big picture of the control environment while driving day-to-day results.
Influence without authority — proven ability to drive compliance and accountability across functions, countries, and levels without direct reporting lines.
Stakeholder management at senior levels — comfortable partnering with Finance Directors, Plant Managers, Country GMs, and external auditors.
Coaching and team development mindset — builds capability, empowers team members, and creates a culture of high performance and continuous learning.
Business acumen — understands that controls should enable the business, not slow it down. Designs solutions that are practical and sustainable.
Adaptability and cultural sensitivity — thrives in a matrixed, multi-country, multicultural environment across 13+ LATAM markets.
Proactive and solution-oriented — doesn't just identify gaps; proposes and implements sustainable fixes.

What We Are NOT Looking For

Candidates with experience only in services (consulting, financial services, BPO) without in-house IC experience in consumer goods or manufacturing.
Candidates with English below fluent B2 — this is non-negotiable regardless of technical strength.
Profiles focused on Internal Audit rather than Internal Controls — these are different functions.
Candidates with no on-site/plant experience — this role requires field presence.

No Relocation support available

Business Unit Summary

Wacam is Mondelēz International’s Latin America presence with more the 1700 wonderful people proudly representing a diversity of cultures and nationalities. Wacam includes 13 countries: Colombia, Ecuador, Perú, Chile, Bolivia, Panamá, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, Guatemela, El Salvador, República Dominicana, Puerto Rico. We make and distribute our global brands and local jewels such as Field, Club Social to over 190 million consumers.

Mondelēz International is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation or preference, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

At Mondelez International we work under a hybrid model, in which our offices at WACAM offer us a space for connection, collaboration and co-creation, with attendance being subject to the needs of the teams themselves and/or the business.

Where permitted by internal policies and local laws, new hires are required to be fully vaccinated with the COVID-19 vaccine as a condition of employment by their date of hire, unless they are granted a medical accommodation.

Introduction

Welcome to Gallagher - a global community of people who bring bold ideas, deep expertise, and a shared commitment to doing what’s right. We help clients navigate complexity with confidence by empowering businesses, communities, and individuals to thrive. At Gallagher, you’ll find more than a job; you’ll find a culture built on trust, driven by collaboration, and sustained by the belief that we’re better together. Experience a workplace where you’re encouraged to be yourself, supported to succeed, and inspired to keep learning. That’s what it means to live The Gallagher Way.

Overview

Join Gallagher’s Corporate Compliance team and help protect the trust people place in our business. In this role, you will support key compliance programs, including conflicts of interest reviews, reporting, testing, and training. Your work will help keep processes clear, timely, and reliable. It will also help teams make informed decisions and meet important standards.

This is a role for someone who likes detail, values good judgment, and wants their work to matter. You will help build a stronger compliance culture across the business. You will also support learning, inclusion, and continuous improvement.

Desde el 16 de julio del 2025 hasta 27 septiembre del 2026 (La implementación interna de la norma inició desde marzo de 2026).
